label: Fundamentals, Architecture & Deployment
desc: 19 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Comparison, Architecture, Ecosystem and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: Apache Flink is an open-source, unified stream- and batch-processing framework created by the Apache Software Foundation.

subs.label: Comparison
subs.desc: Flink's long-term goal is to fully unify batch and streaming, since a bounded dataset can be understood as just a finite stream.

subs.label: Architecture
subs.desc: At its core, Flink is a robust, distributed dataflow engine that executes programs as a stream, using cyclic dataflow execution.

subs.label: Ecosystem
subs.desc: Does Flink need to depend on Hadoop?

subs.label: Use Cases
subs.desc: What are the use cases of Apache Flink? What are the most common types of applications that use Apache Flink?

subs.label: Deployment
subs.desc: What are the different ways to deploy and use Apache Flink? How would you size a Flink cluster for production?

subs.label: Tooling
subs.desc: What are the different types of tools supported by Apache Flink?

label: Programming Model, APIs & Tooling
desc: 18 interview questions covering Programming Model, Architecture, APIs, Libraries and more.

subs.label: Programming Model
subs.desc: What is the Flink programming model? What are the commonly used operators in Flink?

subs.label: Architecture
subs.desc: A slot is a TaskManager-level concept — it determines how many slots a given TaskManager offers, which caps how much parallelism it can support.

subs.label: APIs
subs.desc: The DataStream API handles data as a continuous stream, supporting operations like filtering, routing, windowing, and aggregation.

subs.label: Libraries
subs.desc: FlinkML is Flink's machine learning library — a growing initiative with an expanding set of algorithms and contributors.

subs.label: Ecosystem
subs.desc: What storage systems and streaming sources/sinks does Apache Flink integrate with? What filesystems does Apache Flink support?

subs.label: Tooling
subs.desc: The Flink SQL client provides a command-line interface for running SQL operations — creating and dropping tables, creating and dropping views, and other SQL commands.

label: State, Time, Windowing & Watermarks
desc: 16 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Streams, Time Semantics, Windowing and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: In batch processing, the data is a bounded set with a defined start and end point, so processing only begins once the entire dataset has been ingested.

subs.label: Streams
subs.desc: What are unbounded streams in Apache Flink? What are bounded streams in Apache Flink, and what is bounded vs. unbounded data?

subs.label: Time Semantics
subs.desc: A watermark is Flink's mechanism for handling out-of-order data when working with event time.

subs.label: Windowing
subs.desc: Flink supports dividing a stream into windows based on time or count (a session window is also, conceptually, time-based).

subs.label: State
subs.desc: Flink often needs to store intermediate state during a computation to avoid data loss and support recovery from failure.

subs.label: CEP
subs.desc: A brief introduction to CEP and state programming in Flink.

label: Fault Tolerance, Checkpointing & Operations
desc: 13 interview questions covering Fault Tolerance, Comparison, Performance, Data Quality.

subs.label: Fault Tolerance
subs.desc: For streaming applications, Flink manages fault tolerance by periodically capturing a snapshot of the streaming dataflow's state; if a failure occurs, that snapshot is used to recover.

subs.label: Comparison
subs.desc: How do Spark Streaming and Flink differ in their checkpoint behavior? What is the difference between Spark and Flink serialization?

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: First, confirm the skew: the Flink web UI shows the amount of data each subtask processes, and a serious skew looks like most subtasks handling, say, 100 MB while one handles only 1 MB (or vice versa).

subs.label: Data Quality
subs.desc: How do you handle abnormal (bad) data in Flink?
